result.title: GEMS-RAG: Graph-grounded Engineering Multimodal Standards Retrieval-Augmented Generation
result.summary: Engineering standards are challenging knowledge sources for large language models (LLMs) because they are hierarchical, multimodal, and densely connected through figures, tables, cross-references, and normative rules. Existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods often rely on unstructured text retrieval and struggle with questions requiring joint reasoning over textual provisions, visual specifications, and document structure. We propose GEMS-RAG (Graph-grounded Engineering Multimodal Standards Retrieval-Augmented Generation), a framework for grounded reasoning over engineering standards. GEMS-RAG combines hierarchical parsing, fine-grained visual entity extraction, multimodal knowledge graph construction, and graph-grounded hybrid retrieval. Instead of treating figures as monolithic images, it decomposes them into meaningful visual entities linked to textual provisions, engineering concepts, and regulatory rules. During inference, dense, sparse, and visual retrieval are combined with graph expansion to identify relevant evidence across text, figures, and document structure. We evaluate GEMS-RAG on the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (MUTCD), a large engineering standard containing egulations, technical drawings, and standardized traffic-control devices. Results show that graph-grounded multimodal retrieval improves retrieval effectiveness and question-answering performance over text-only, multimodal, and graph-based RAG baselines. Beyond MUTCD, GEMS-RAG offers a general framework for reasoning over engineering codes, technical manuals, regulatory documents, and scientific standards in safety-critical applications.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GEMS-RAG，将工程标准文档做层次化解析，把图表拆成细粒度视觉实体并与文本条款、规则一起构建多模态知识图谱，推理时用稠密、稀疏、视觉检索结合图扩展选取证据，在 MUTCD 上评测问答效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把图像拆成可链接文本条款的视觉实体」加图扩展混合检索的思路，可能为 VLM 推理中的视觉证据筛选与结构化证据组织提供可核查线索；但属文档级 RAG，未涉及 latent 状态或推理期状态生成。
